spec.hypothesis: With batch 128 and learning rate 0.08, a tanh or ReLU hidden activation may change validation macro F1 compared with sigmoid within 100 epochs; He initialization may change ReLU results compared with Xavier.

timing_benchmark.design: Each round trains every configuration for 5 epochs from its seed-42 initial model; the order rotates every round (sigmoid, tanh, relu-xavier, relu-he; then tanh first; then relu-xavier first). Quality is not measured.

notes: Campaign epoch timings are not comparable: the machine slept during sigmoid-xavier seed 44 (epochs 96-99) and tanh-xavier seed 42 (19 epochs), and later runs used battery power. The analyzer clock counts sleep. Use timing_benchmark for speed.
Losses, checkpoints and scores are unaffected by sleep: training is deterministic for a given seed and standard library.

Seeds are reproducible on the same C++ standard library only: std::shuffle (epoch order) and std::normal_distribution (He initialization) give different sequences with libc++ (macOS) and libstdc++ (Linux); std::uniform_real_distribution (Xavier) matched in a direct check.
